items.problem: At 390px the model catalog — the site's primary surface — shows the MODEL column and nothing else. Every column a reader consults a price catalogue FOR (in/mtok, out/mtok, context, status) is off-screen to the right inside a horizontally scrolling container. The reflow oracle confirms the mechanism rather than contradicting it: at a 320px viewport it measured 'thead 1112px; tr 1112px', i.e. the table keeps its full desktop width and hides roughly 760px of it behind a container scroll. The page-level check passes (R2 is satisfied) while the surface is functionally empty: 13,843px of scrolling that delivers 396 names and no numbers. A mobile reader cannot compare two models' prices without horizontally scrolling each row independently, which destroys the row alignment that made comparison possible.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/table-catalog--light--390.png (and the 320px reflow line in scripts/verify-design.mjs output: 'no horizontal scroll at 320px /catalog — thead 1112px; tr 1112px')
items.invariant: At 390px the /catalog listing shall present, without horizontal scrolling, the model name AND at least the input price, output price and lifecycle status for each row.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R2 — R2 requires wide content to scroll inside its own container rather than the page, and this remedy stays inside it: the fix is to stop the table being wide at 390px (a stacked or reduced-column presentation), not to let the page scroll. R2 is satisfied today and must remain satisfied.
items.prescription: Below the existing 33.999rem breakpoint in globals.css, drop .data-table out of table layout into a stacked record-per-row presentation: model name as the row heading, then a compact label/value grid for in/out/context/status. Alternatively keep a table but render a prioritised 3-column subset (model, in/mtok, out/mtok) with the remainder in a per-row disclosure. Either satisfies the invariant; the stacked form is likelier to hold at 320px too.

items.problem: Structure is carried by borders, not by type and space. Every list on the site draws a 1px rule under every row — 396 on /catalog, roughly 85 on /wiki, 24 on the home changed-feed, 12 on the /tools jump list, 11 on /data — and /catalog additionally draws a box around the whole table. On top of that, .badge puts a bordered uppercase chip on EVERY row including the default state: roughly 60 grey 'ACTIVE' chips on /wiki and 396 on /catalog, all saying the same thing. A badge that appears on every row carries no information; it is decoration, and it dilutes the ember-toned DEAD/RETIRED/DEPRECATED chips that do carry meaning. The cost is higher in dark: --rule #2c303b against --paper #14161c reads as a stronger ladder than #d7d8e0 on #f6f6f8 does in light, so the same chrome budget is over-spent in the dark theme. The site already contains the correct pattern — /learn rules only at level boundaries, uses no badges, and is the most scannable page on the property.
items.invariant: A list row shall not carry a bottom rule and a status chip simultaneously; and a status indicator shall render only for rows whose status differs from the collection's default.
items.governing_rule: null — checked R1 through R6; none governs divider density or badge policy. R1 constrains contrast only, and the remedy removes marks rather than adding low-contrast ones, so it cannot regress R1.
items.prescription: In globals.css, remove border-bottom from .browse-row and .data-table tbody tr and let the existing 0.35rem padding plus a single --rule-strong line under the header carry the group. Render .badge only when data-tone is set (ended/early/theme); for the default 'active' state emit nothing, or plain --muted mono text with no border and no background.

items.problem: The templates do not share a grid. Against a --shell of 76rem (1216px) with a consistent 145px left margin, the content's RIGHT edge lands in three different places depending on template: about 1295px on /catalog, /wiki and /data (full shell), about 1000px on /learn (rail plus column), and about 750px on /blog/*, /wiki/* and /colophon (--measure, 38rem). Nothing occupies the difference — no sidenotes, no table of contents, no secondary rail — so a reader moving between two pages of one property sees the text block change width by 545px with no signal that anything changed. Link treatment drifts the same way across the three index templates: /catalog sets model names in accent plus underline, /wiki sets entry names in plain --ink with no underline at all, /blog sets post titles in accent bold with no underline. Three indexes, three conventions for the same act of clicking a row.
items.invariant: Every page template shall place its primary content column against one of at most two declared grid tracks, and a row-title link shall use one identical resting treatment (colour and underline) on every index template.
items.governing_rule: null — checked R1 through R6; none constrains grid or link treatment. R6 pins home-page above-the-fold content only and is unaffected by column geometry.
items.prescription: Declare two tracks in globals.css and use only those: a reading track at --measure and a full track at --shell, with prose templates either centring the reading track inside the shell or filling the residue with the page's own structured data (see I5). Then unify the row-title link: pick one of the three existing treatments — accent colour, no underline at rest — and apply it to .browse-name, the /catalog model cell and the /blog post title alike.

items.target: shared design system (app/globals.css, .browse-row) — consumed by /wiki and /data
items.problem: .browse-row is 'grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) auto auto', so the name column absorbs the entire shell and welds the type and status cells to the far right edge. On /wiki at 1440 the entry name ends around x=215 and its type ('concept', 'org', 'model') begins around x=1170 — roughly 950px of empty row between a value and the attribute that describes it, repeated for 85 rows. The reader must traverse the full page width to associate each name with its kind, or track along a rule. The same shape recurs on /data, where 'Entries — identity, lifecycle, indexability' sits at the left margin and '/dataset/entries.csv' at the right with about 700px of nothing between. That the layout is wrong rather than merely wide is settled by the site's own 390px rendering of the identical component, where name and badge sit adjacent and the row reads correctly, and by /colophon, whose Records/Catalog/Change-history block packs label and value into a tight left-aligned pair. The system already contains the right idiom and the index templates use the wrong one.
items.invariant: In a two-value list row, the horizontal gap between the end of the primary value and the start of its associated attribute shall not exceed the width of the primary value column's longest entry.
items.governing_rule: null — checked R1 through R6; none constrains column distribution. The remedy narrows a grid and cannot affect R2, which the row already satisfies.
items.prescription: Change .browse-row to a bounded track set — e.g. 'minmax(0, 32rem) auto auto' with 'justify-content: start' — so the name column stops at its content and type and status follow immediately after it, leaving the residue at the right of the row rather than inside it. Apply the same bounding to the /data listing rows.

items.problem: The wiki entry is the site's answer surface, and it buries its answer. On /wiki/concept/ai-winter the FACTS block — term origin, lighthill report, alpac report, symbolics revenue trend, each with its source and accessed date — is the structured payload a reference reader arrived for, and it sits at roughly y=2400 of a 2937px page, after every word of prose. Meanwhile the body column is capped at --measure (605px) inside a 1216px shell, so 545px of column runs empty down the entire length of that prose. The page simultaneously has nowhere to put the facts and 545px of unused width beside them. The same shape holds on /blog/* where the title and its meta rule span the full 1150px but the body that follows is 605px, so the page's own header promises a column width the content does not deliver.
items.invariant: On a wiki entry at 1440px, the FACTS block shall be reachable without scrolling past the full prose body — either rendered in the residual column beside the prose or placed above it.
items.governing_rule: null — checked R1 through R6. R6 governs the home page only; this is the analogous intent-preservation concern for entry pages and should become a numbered rule if this item is accepted. NOTE: moving the FACTS block is a RESTRUCTURE, so it is subject to keeper point KP1 and needs a before/after pair approved before it commits.
items.prescription: At 64rem and above, lay the entry as 'grid-template-columns: minmax(0, var(--measure)) minmax(0, 1fr)' and move the FACTS definition list into the second track, sticky to the top of the prose. This spends the dead 545px on the page's highest-value content and satisfies the invariant without changing a word. Do not change which facts appear or how they are worded.

items.problem: On the /wiki index the 85 entry names are set in plain --ink with 'text-decoration: none', and acquire accent colour and an underline only on :hover. At rest — the state every screenshot in the stack captures, and the state a reader sees before moving the mouse — nothing distinguishes a clickable entry from static text. The wiki index is the site's alphabetical front door to 495 records and it presents as a printed list. This is not an axe violation and axe passed cleanly on the sampled routes, so the measured oracle is silent on it by design; and hover is a declared screenshot blind spot, which is precisely why the resting state is the one that must carry the affordance.
items.invariant: Every row-title link shall be distinguishable from non-interactive text by colour or underline in its resting state, without hover or focus.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R1 — checked: R1 requires zero axe violations, which the current treatment already satisfies, so this is not an R1 failure. Any remedy must keep the new resting colour above the contrast threshold R1 enforces in BOTH themes; --accent (#4a3bd4 in light) already clears it as used on /blog.
items.prescription: Give .browse-name 'color: var(--accent)' at rest, matching the treatment /blog already uses for post titles, and reserve the underline for hover. This also discharges half of I3's link-consistency invariant.

items.problem: Two elements claim 'position: sticky; top: 0' in the same scroll context. '.site-header' is sticky at top:0 with z-index 10, and '.data-table thead th' is also sticky at top:0 with no z-index. On /catalog — a 13,427px table — the column headers will therefore stick underneath the site header and be occluded, so the sticky header that exists to keep MODEL / IN / OUT / CONTEXT visible across 396 rows does not do it. The screenshot stack cannot show this: every capture is a full-page render of the document at scroll position zero, where both elements sit at their natural position and the collision has not yet occurred. Flagged from the token system I was invited to read; the observability gap is filed separately as I13.
items.evidence: app/globals.css lines ~198-201 (.site-header) and ~858-862 (.data-table thead th); no capture in loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/ can show a scrolled state — see I13
items.invariant: When /catalog is scrolled past its first rows, the table's column headers shall remain fully visible and unoccluded by the site header.
items.governing_rule: null — checked R1 through R6; none covers sticky stacking. R2 is unaffected: the change is vertical offset and z-index only.
items.prescription: Set '.data-table thead th { top: var(--header-h); z-index: 5 }' with --header-h declared from the actual site-header height, keeping it below the site header's z-index 10. Verify with a scrolled capture once I13 lands. If the collision turns out not to occur, decline with cause and record it as a known evidence lie.

items.problem: The catalog's READ column renders the identical string '2026-08-31' on all 396 rows, in accent colour, as an independent link. A column whose every cell holds the same value discriminates nothing; it consumes a seventh of the table's width and adds a second full column of accent to a table that already sets its model names in accent, so two of seven columns are entirely coloured and the ember that marks a genuinely deprecated row has to compete with them. It is also the direct cause of the route's tab burden: the traversal oracle counted 817 focusable elements on /catalog, which is 396 model links plus 396 date links plus controls. A keyboard reader crossing the catalog passes through two stops per row where one would do, and that duplication is what exhausts the focus sweep in I12.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/table-catalog--light--1440.png, table-catalog--dark--1440.png; scripts/verify-design.mjs output: '/catalog — 150 of 817 focusable element(s)'
items.invariant: A /catalog column in which every row holds an identical value shall not be rendered as a per-row column, and /catalog shall expose at most one focusable element per data row.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R4 and R5 — checked: R4 requires nav, search and toggle to be reachable and activatable, and R5 requires a focus indicator on every stop; removing 396 redundant links keeps both satisfied and makes R5's full sweep achievable within the rig's cap. Removing the column does not remove information from the page, so slot 1's content prohibition is not engaged — the same date is already stated once in the page header ('last checked 2026-08-31'). If the implementer judges otherwise, decline and route to the keeper.
items.prescription: Drop the per-row READ column and state the read date once, in the table caption or the existing header line that already carries 'last checked 2026-08-31'. Where a row's read date genuinely differs from the collection's, show it on that row only — the same exception-only principle as I2. Reclaim the freed width for the price columns.

items.problem: The home page's right rail stops at roughly y=480 while the changed-feed beside it continues to y=1120, leaving about 640px of empty column in the middle of the site's front door, in both themes. The rail carries the property's highest-value orientation content — the 396-model catalog count, the deprecated-and-retired list, the latest post and latest tutorial — and it occupies under 40% of the height available to it before the layout drops back to full width. The feed's own rows meanwhile have ragged heights because the trailing 'source' link wraps to a second line on roughly half of them, so the two-column band reads as neither a settled grid nor a continuous list.
items.invariant: The home page's secondary rail shall not terminate more than one feed-row height above the end of the primary feed column beside it.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R6 — checked and binding: R6 requires changed-feed lines visible above the fold at 1440x900 and 390x844, currently passing at 12 and 4 lines. Any rebalancing of this band must keep both counts non-zero. NOTE: this is a RESTRUCTURE and therefore subject to KP1.
items.prescription: Either extend the rail with content already present elsewhere on the page — the 'EVERYTHING HERE' section that currently sits below the feed is the obvious candidate, and moving it into the rail fills the void and shortens the page without adding or changing copy — or end the two-column band where the rail ends and let the feed run full width below it. Separately, give the feed row a fixed grid so 'source' occupies a right-aligned track instead of wrapping.

items.problem: There is no @font-face, no next/font and no bundled face anywhere in app/. Type is '--serif: Charter, Bitstream Charter, Sitka Text, Cambria, Georgia, Times New Roman, serif' plus a system mono stack. The serif/mono split itself is a genuinely good domain choice — serif for argument, mono for every dated machine-read fact — and it is applied with discipline. The defect is the fallback chain: Charter, Sitka Text, Cambria, Georgia and Times New Roman differ materially in x-height and set width, so the same page resolves to a different face on macOS, Windows and Linux. The controlled 38rem measure therefore yields a different character count per platform, and the vertical rhythm built on --step--1 through --step-4 lands on different baselines, which means the typographic system the rest of this verdict credits is only actually true on machines that happen to have Charter installed.
items.evidence: app/globals.css lines 55-57 and the absence of any @font-face across app/; rendering visible in loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/article--light--1440.png and prose--light--1440.png
items.invariant: The resolved body face shall be identical across platforms — either self-hosted, or a stack whose fallbacks are metric-compatible with the primary via size-adjust.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R3 — checked and binding: first-load payload must stay under 150 KB gzipped. The current worst route is 122.3 KB, leaving about 27 KB of headroom. Note that R3 as written measures JavaScript, so a woff2 face would not count against it as currently specified; say so explicitly rather than assuming, and prefer a subset under 30 KB either way.
items.prescription: Self-host one subset woff2 for the serif (Charter is openly licensed) with font-display: swap and a size-adjust-tuned local fallback, so the measure and rhythm resolve identically everywhere. If R3 is read to cover total payload rather than JS alone, subset to Latin plus the figures actually used.

items.problem: Every /tools listing renders the same four fields for all 35 entries — licence, pricing model, verification date and link — as a single run-on mono line separated by middots, wrapping to two lines at the full 1150px width. The fields are identical in kind across every entry, which is the definition of tabular data, but they are set as 35 sentences of differing length. A reader comparing what each tool costs must read 35 prose runs instead of scanning one column. The site already demonstrates it can do this correctly: /catalog aligns the same class of data into columns.
items.invariant: Where every entry in a listing carries the same set of fields, those fields shall be presented in aligned columns rather than as a delimited run of inline text.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R2 — checked: any columnar treatment must not introduce page-level horizontal scroll at 320px, which /tools currently passes; the mobile form must collapse to stacked label/value, and must not repeat I1's failure of hiding columns behind a container scroll.
items.prescription: Give .listing a grid of name / licence / pricing / verified tracks bounded well inside the shell, aligning the four fields down the page within each category section. Below 33.999rem, stack them as label/value pairs. This is a presentation change only: the same strings appear, in the same order, under the same headings.

items.problem: The focus-indicator sweep on /catalog reports 'PASS — 150 of 817 focusable element(s) — STOPPED AT THE 150-STOP CAP, the rest unswept'. It records a PASS having examined 18% of the route, and the 667 unexamined stops are precisely the deep-table region most likely to differ from the header region that was swept. This is the exact failure mode R5's own preserved post-mortem was written to prevent — 'a check that stops early passes for the wrong reason' — reappearing as a cap instead of an early return. R5 additionally requires that a traversal assert the number of stops it visited and compare that count against the page's actual focusable count: the check does compute and print both numbers, they disagree by 667, and it still records PASS. The artifact may well be fine here; the oracle cannot currently say so, and it is claiming that it can.
items.evidence: scripts/verify-design.mjs output, focus indicators section: '/catalog — 150 of 817 focusable element(s) — STOPPED AT THE 150-STOP CAP, the rest unswept'
items.prescription: Do not change the artifact for this item. Make the sweep record FAIL, or a distinct INCOMPLETE outcome that does not count as a pass, whenever swept is less than focusable. If the 150-stop cap exists for runtime reasons, replace exhaustive sweeping with a sample that always includes the last stop and a random interior stop, and report the sampling explicitly in the output line. Note that I8, if accepted, cuts /catalog from 817 stops to roughly 421 and makes a full sweep cheaper.

items.problem: All 40 captures are full-page renders of the document at scroll position zero. Nothing in the stack can show any state that exists only after scrolling, which on this site includes both sticky elements: the site header and the /catalog table head. I7 identifies a probable collision between them from the CSS alone, and the screenshot class the charter declares valid for table craft can neither confirm nor refute it. The blind spot is partly named in the oracle table as 'anything below the captured fold', but a full-page capture is easy to mistake for coverage of the scrolled state, because it does show the content that lies below the fold — just never in its scrolled configuration.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/manifest.json (40 entries, every one a full-page top-of-document capture) and the absence of any scrolled capture for the 13,427px /catalog page
items.prescription: Do not change the artifact for this item. Add one viewport-sized capture per long route taken after scrolling about 1200px — /catalog and one wiki entry are sufficient — labelled distinctly (e.g. table-catalog--light--1440--scrolled.png) so sticky and header-occlusion behaviour becomes a judgeable evidence class. Add 'a full-page capture does not show the scrolled configuration of sticky elements' to JUDGE.md's Known evidence lies.

items.problem: The /catalog page presents 396 rows as one continuous 13,427px table with four filter controls and no pagination or grouping beyond an A-to-Z sort within provider. Whether a reader who arrives knowing only 'I want a cheap long-context model' can actually converge on one is a question about that reader's behaviour, not about the pixels: the filters may be entirely sufficient, or the row count may defeat them. No screenshot answers it, and the axe, reflow, payload and traversal oracles are all silent on it. Filed so it stops resurfacing as an actionable layout finding — the density and column work in I1 and I8 should not be justified by findability claims this loop cannot test.
items.prescription: Keeper decision. Resolving it needs a real reader attempting a real lookup, which is outside this loop's oracle stack. If the keeper wants it closed, the cheapest instrument is a timed task with three people, not another screenshot.
